(i) chiral perturbation is a reliable tool to extrapolate lattice results to the physical point, (ii) the PCR is small, (iii) FRR is a reliable method to extend the PCR, and (iv) the PCR is not the same as the region of applicability of the chiral effective theory.

the extrapolation of lattice Q CD results beyond the PCR.

the extrapolation problem in chiral effective field theories, which is the problem of how to use lattice results to constrain the low-energy constants (LECs) in the effective field theory and how to use these LECs to extrapolate to physical pion mass and/or to the continuum limit.
the extrapolation of QCD results beyond their power-counting regime, and with the development and testing of resummation techniques to accomplish this task.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chiral expansion of QCD is convergent, but that its convergence is very slow.
the chiral expansion of lattice QCD is a useful tool to extrapolate lattice QCD results to the physical pion and kaon masses, but not to the physical masses of the heavier mesons.
chiral perturbation is an excellent approximation to QCD at small pion masses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chiral expansion works, but the PCR is very small.
chiral perturbation theories are very useful for lattice QCD, and that lattice simulations are essential to constrain and test chiral perturbation expansions.
chiral effective field theories are very useful for making contact with lattice simulation results of hadrons, but they have their limitations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lattice simulation results of QCD are already beyond the PCR, and that resummation techniques are required to make accurate contact between lattice results and QCD.
lattice simulation results are consistent with chiral perturbation theories only in the PCR.
lattice simulations must reach the chiral regime to make reliable contact with the continuum limit.
